newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures drift to mixed close.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures drift to mixed close.

text.p: IMM currency futures drifted to a mixed close after quiet afternoon pit trading.
Nearby marks and yen slipped again near the close as traders evened positions after mainly calm late activity.
"It's been very quiet, mostly rollover," said one floor broker during the final 30 minutes. "Outside of that, we haven't seen much in the outrights."

March 1997 futures became new lead-month contracts on Monday and players who still hold December 1996 contracts, which stop trading next Monday morning, began rolling those into the March listing in earnest today.

Brokers said spreading by one French-owned firm in particular pumped up morning volume. The firm was seen selling some 6,000 mark, more than 2,000 Swiss franc and as many as 3,000 sterling December/March spreads.
The market glossed over midmorning comments by French president Jacques Chirac and German chancellor Helmut Kohl, who said jointly neither nation wants a weak euro currency.

Kohl added that it makes no sense to speculate on which nations would be initial members of the currency union. He also said EU finance ministers were still preparing for stability pact talks in Dublin this weekend.

The Swiss unit, which edged off further versus the mark, also lost ground after early morning remarks by Swiss National Bank board member Jean-Pierre Roth. He said the central bank was "pleased" with the Swiss franc's recent decline from levels he described as "not very realistic" and that the SNB was sticking to its current monetary strategy.
Technicals also weighed down the Swiss unit, traders said.

"I think the Swiss (franc) after last week had been jerked around and now is going in the direction it was expected to go," said another floor broker. "I didn't expect it to move this much today, but there's still a bit more downside."
He pegged a nearterm target for the dollar/Swiss franc at 1.3325, or about $0.7573 basis March futures and about $0.7514 in December futures.
The impending holidays, coupled with yearend book-closings, could keep volumes scanty and contribute to wider price swings, brokers added.
"After last week, with its moves, if they have profits locked in, they're going to be cautious...." the broker added.
Currencies regrouped over the weekend after last week's gyrations spawned by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's comments about irrational exuberance affecting stock values.
Subsequent remarks by world economic leaders helped temper the market's reaction, which traders agreed had been overdone.

March yen ended down $0.000035 at $0.008939, marks fell $0.0043 to $0.6460, Swiss lost $0.0068 to $0.7600, sterling rose $0.0020 to $1.6446, Canadian dollar rose $0.0033 to $0.7428, Aussie dollar jumped $0.0079 to $0.8024, Mexican peso rose $0.000850 to $0.120075.
